Technology stocks were little changed this afternoon, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 losing about 0.1% in value today while the Philadelphia semiconductor index was posting a nearly 0.3% gain.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ Bilibili ( BILI ) still was surging late in Thursday trading after the Chinese mobile games and entertainment platform narrowed its Q1 net loss compared with the year-ago period and revenue more than doubling over last year. Excluding one-time item, net loss for the three months ended March 31 was RMB0.94 per American depository share, or about $0.15 per share, compared with an RMB1.58 per ADS net loss during the same quarter last year. Total net revenue rose nearly 105% year over year to RMB868.0 million from RMB424.1 million during the first three months of 2017. Analyst estimates weren't available for comparison. Analyst estimates were not available for comparison but after the improved Q1 results, analysts at Bank of America Merrill Lynch raised their price target for Bilibili ADS by $2.30 to $15.30 apiece while also reiterating their Buy rating for the stock.
In other sector news:
+ Verint Systems ( VRNT ) was about 2% higher in late Thursday trading after saying its FaceDetect biometrics technology recently was named a gold-level winner in video analytics by the Security Today online news platform as part of the 2018 Government Security Awards. The advanced face-recognition technology also received an honorable mention in the video analytics category during the Security Industry Association's recent New Product Showcase.
- DHI Group ( DHX ) was down over 1% Thursday afternoon after the technology and data services provider saying it sold its Hcareers job board for the hospitality industry to Virgil Holdings, the owner and operator of Virgil Careers, a hiring and recruiting platform using proprietary machine learning and micro-assessments to match job seekers with employers. Terms of the transaction were not disclosed.
- QuickLogic ( QUIK ) dropped to a nine-year low on Thursday, losing almost one-third of its former value to touch its worst share price since February 2009 at $1.05 apiece after the chipmaker priced a $15.5 million public offering of more than 13.5 million shares of its common stock at $1.15 apiece, or about a 26.3% discount to Wednesday's closing price for the company's stock. Investors in the deal also received a five-year warrant to buy an additional 0.4 of a share for each share they purchased in the stock sale. The warrants have an exercise price of $1.38 a share. Quicklogic expects to use net proceeds from the offering for working capital, developing new products and general corporate purposes.
